blocks.text: Embarking on the journey of Mahābhārata is in itself experiencing the physical presence of the divine in our life. The accounts of Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, Maharṣi Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa, Bhārgavarāma, Balarāmā, Devavrata-Bhīṣma or Maharṣi Animāndavyā, among many more, are awe-inspiring moments of reading. When Devavrata makes that fierce and terrible vow, the skies thunder with the voices of the Gods, "Bhīṣma... Bhīṣma...". When the Pāṇḍavas are born, all the devas appear in the sky and shower them with blessings and flowers (Whereas when Duryodhana is born, a donkey brays outside, and the minster suggests that this being a bad sign, he should be abandoned then and there to save the kingdom).
